questions.question: Who shares responsibility for platform email security under the Shared Responsibility Model?
questions.explanation:
In the Shared Responsibility Model, the customer shares responsibility for platform email security. They configure security when they integrate ServiceNow email. They set up accounts and protocols (SMTP/IMAP/POP3). They enable authentication and TLS. They define routing and allowlists. They align instance settings with their security and compliance policies.
 In the Shared Responsibility Model, ServiceNow shares responsibility by securing the underlying platform components that process and relay email, including the SaaS platform's infrastructure, mail-handling services, availability, patching, and baseline security controls. ServiceNow hardens and monitors the platform so that email messages handled by the instance are protected by the platform's built-in security posture and compliance practices.
 In the Shared Responsibility Model, the colocation facility is limited to the physical layer; power, cooling, racks, and building access controls, and does not participate in configuring or enforcing email security controls within a ServiceNow instance, so it is not a party to platform email security responsibilities.
 In the Shared Responsibility Model, the cloud service provider operates the cloud infrastructure; compute, storage, network fabric, and hypervisors, that hosts the SaaS environment but does not manage or set email security policies inside the ServiceNow instance; platform-and tenant-level email security responsibilities sit with ServiceNow and the customer, respectively.
 In the Shared Responsibility Model, email system administrators manage the organization's external mail systems and services and may provide SMTP credentials used by ServiceNow to those systems, but they do not configure or secure the ServiceNow platform's internal email security controls; their scope remains outside the platform boundary and does not replace the shared responsibilities between ServiceNow and the customer.
questions.topic: Database Management and Platform Security - Shared Responsibility Model

questions.question: In what state is a Knowledge article when it becomes visible to end users?
questions.explanation:
A knowledge article must be in the Published state to be visible to end users. The Published state makes the article active and available through the knowledge base.
 Articles in the Retired state do not appear to end users. This state indicates the article is no longer relevant or has been removed from general availability.
 Articles in the Draft state are not visible to end users. Draft is used for authors to begin creating or updating an article before it is reviewed or published.
 Articles in the Review state are not shown to end users. Review is used when an article is awaiting approval or edits before it can be published.
questions.topic: Self Service & Automation - Knowledge Management

questions.question: Which statement about coalesce in Import Sets is true?
options: Coalesce deletes the existing record when the values do not match.
Coalesce requires the sys_id field to be used as the match criteria.
Coalesce prevents new records from being created during a transform.
Coalesce updates an existing record when a matching value is found in the target table.
questions.explanation:
Coalesce updates an existing record when a matching value is found in the target table. Coalesce causes the transform process to look for a target table record whose field matches the import set row. If a match exists, that record is updated.
 Coalesce does not delete existing records when the values do not match. When no matching value is found in the target table, the transform process creates a new record instead of deleting one.
 Coalesce does not require sys_id to be used as the match criteria. Coalesce can be set on any field, and administrators may designate one or multiple fields for matching.
 Coalesce does not prevent new records from being created during a transform. If no match is found in the target table, the transform process automatically creates a new record.
questions.topic: Database Management and Platform Security - Importing Data

questions.question: Which modules are used to change the banner image?
questions.explanation:
The Basic Configuration UI16 module provides a centralized way to modify key branding elements of the classic UI, including the banner image, header colors, and system title. Administrators can upload or reference a new image from this module to update the banner that appears across the UI16 interface.
 The My Company module can also be used to change the banner image. The Company record contains the UI16 Banner Image field, which ServiceNow evaluates when deciding which logo or banner to display in the header. Updating the UI16 Banner Image field on the My Company record updates the logo used across the UI, and this method takes precedence over other logo sources in the platform's resolution order.
 UI Policies cannot be used to change the banner image. They are designed to manage form behavior such as field visibility, mandatory settings, and read-only conditions. Their scope is limited strictly to form logic and does not extend to UI-level branding or image configuration, and there is no mechanism within UI Policies to alter banner images or system-wide UI elements.
 The Cascading Style Sheets (CSS) module cannot be used to change the banner image. This module is intended for overriding or extending CSS styling rules rather than replacing UI components or uploaded images. While CSS scripts can apply styling to elements, ServiceNow's documented process for banner image changes requires updating a defined system property or company record rather than using CSS overrides.
 The Maintain Items module cannot be used to change the banner image. This module operates within the catalog application and does not interact with UI branding, which is controlled through system properties, theme configuration, or the Company record.
questions.topic: Instance Configuration - Personalizing/customizing the instance

questions.question: Which feature allows users to narrow down the records displayed in a list by applying specific conditions?
questions.explanation:
The filter feature allows users to narrow down the records displayed in a list by applying specific conditions. Filters let users define criteria so only matching records are shown.
 A tag does not narrow down the records displayed in a list. Tags are used to label or categorize records so users can easily find or group them later.
 The activity stream does not narrow down the records displayed in a list. The activity stream shows comments, work notes, and record history for a specific record.
 A favorite does not narrow down the records displayed in a list. Favorites allow users to bookmark frequently accessed lists, modules, or records for quick navigation.
questions.topic: Configuring Applications for Collaboration - Lists, Filters, and Tags

questions.question: What are key aspects of a Service in the CSDM?
questions.explanation:
Interaction represents how users engage with the service and is one of the three components defined in the Common Service Data Model (CSDM) service model.
 Offering represents the units of value delivered to customers and is defined as a core component of a service in the CSDM.
 A portfolio organizes and categorizes services but is not one of the three foundational components of a service in the CSDM. Operating models describe organizational structures and processes but are not components of a service in the CSDM.
 An asset is a tracked resource, not one of the three conceptual components of a service.
questions.topic: Database Management and Platform Security - CMDB and CSDM

questions.question: Which icon provides access to configuration options such as Form Layout and Related Lists?
questions.explanation:
The form context menu icon provides access to configuration options such as Form Layout, Related Lists, and other form personalization settings. The form context menu icon allows Administrators to customize how fields, sections, and related information appear on a form. The Application Navigator icon does not provide form configuration options. It is used to browse and open applications and modules in the platform.
 The More actions icon does not provide form configuration options. It is used to toggle the template bar or annotations.
 The Activity Stream icon does not provide form configuration options. It is used to view comments, work notes, and record history on a form.
questions.topic: Configuring Applications for Collaboration - Form Configuration

questions.question: What allows a user to navigate back to a page record they were recently on?
questions.explanation:
History allows users to return to recently visited records, lists, and pages, giving them quick access to previously viewed items.
 Favorites does not take a user back to a recently visited record. Favorites allow a user to save frequently accessed modules or pages for easy access.
 The Application Picker does not help users return to recently viewed pages. The Application Picker allows a user to change the development scope when working in Studio or configuring applications.
 The User Menu does not bring a user back to a recently viewed record. The User Menu allows a user to access personal settings, profile options, and impersonation features.
questions.topic: Platform Overview and Navigation - Next Experience Unified Navigation

questions.question: Which statement describes Security Center?
options: Security Center replaces role-based access control with a user friendly UI.
Security Center can improve security posture and strengthen compliance levels.
Security Center seamlessly manages MFA for the instance.
Security Center can automate recommended security changes.
questions.explanation:
Security Center centralizes risk insights, security scoring, and actionable recommendations, enabling administrators to continuously improve their instance's security posture and strengthen compliance. Security Center provides a unified, intuitive view of critical issues, recommended remediations, and configuration gaps, helping teams proactively address risks without manually searching across disparate security settings. By consolidating visibility and guidance into a single workspace, Security Center supports a more consistent and efficient approach to maintaining a secure and compliant ServiceNow environment.
 Security Center provides prioritized recommendations and step-by-step remediation guidance but does not automatically apply or enforce configuration changes. Administrators remain responsible for reviewing each recommendation, deciding whether it is appropriate for their environment, and manually performing the required updates. This design ensures full administrative control and prevents unintentional automatic changes that could affect business logic or security configurations.
 Security Center does not alter or replace role-based access control (RBAC), nor does it override Access Control Lists (ACLs). Standard ACL rules continue to determine which users can view or modify data, regardless of the Security Center interface. Although Security Center provides an improved, consolidated user experience for assessing security risks, it does not change the underlying access control mechanisms that govern permissions throughout the platform.
 Security Center does not manage multi-factor authentication (MFA) or oversee authentication workflows. All authentication functions, including MFA configuration, single sign-on (SSO), and identity provider integrations, remain part of Access Management. While Security Center helps administrators monitor security posture, MFA settings are still controlled independently through authentication configuration pages and are not part of Security Center's capabilities.
questions.topic: Database Management and Platform Security - Security Center

questions.question: Which language is primarily used in ServiceNow?
questions.explanation:
JavaScript is the primary scripting language used across the ServiceNow platform. It powers both client-side logic, such as Client Scripts, UI Policies with script actions, and Catalog Client Scripts, and server-side logic including Business Rules, Script Includes, Scheduled Jobs, and Workflow Scripts. ServiceNow's official scripting model, including its Glide APIs, is built entirely around JavaScript, making it the foundational language for customization and automation on the platform.
 Python is not used as a scripting language within the ServiceNow platform. Instead, Python is used externally when integrating with ServiceNow through REST or SOAP web services. ServiceNow provides examples of Python clients for interacting with platform APIs, demonstrating Python's role as an integration tool rather than a native scripting language.
 Jelly Script is not the primary scripting language in ServiceNow. Jelly is a markup-based templating technology used mainly in older or legacy UI components such as UI Pages and UI Macros. It serves as a rendering layer for generating HTML and form layouts rather than for process automation or business logic.
 HTML is not a scripting language in ServiceNow. HTML is a markup language used strictly for structuring and presenting content within UI Pages, Now Experience components, or catalog HTML variables. It provides visual layout capabilities but does not control platform logic or automation.
questions.topic: Data Migration and Integration - Scripting in ServiceNow

questions.question: Which components of an Access Control rule are mandatory when defining an ACL?
questions.explanation:
Type is mandatory. Every Access Control rule (ACL) must identify whether it is a table-level or field-level rule. Without the Type, the ACL engine cannot determine the scope of the access check.
 Name is mandatory. Every ACL must specify the table or field it governs. The ACL engine relies on the Name to determine where the rule applies. Applies to is not mandatory. Applies to is not required for either table-level or field-level ACLs.
 Advanced is not mandatory. It only enables script-based evaluation when selected. An ACL can be defined using roles or conditions without enabling the Advanced option.
 Admin overrides is not mandatory. It simply determines whether administrators bypass the rule. An ACL can be created without enabling this option, and it does not affect whether the rule is valid or defined correctly.
questions.topic: Database Management and Platform Security - Application/Access Control

questions.question: How is access to a knowledge base managed?
questions.explanation:
User Criteria control access to a knowledge base and its articles. They determine which users can view, contribute to, or manage knowledge content based on specific attributes such as roles, groups, or user fields.
 Managing access to a knowledge base is not a functionality of UI Policies. UI Policies change the visibility, ability to edit, and mandatory status of fields on forms based on conditions.
 Managing access to a knowledge base is not a functionality of Client Scripts. Client Scripts run in the user's browser to validate data or modify form behavior.
 Managing access to a knowledge base is not a functionality of Business Rules. Business Rules run on the server to enforce data logic or automation.
questions.topic: Self Service & Automation - Knowledge Management

questions.question: What are the behaviors that occur once a flow has been triggered?
questions.explanation:
Actions are the operations a flow performs after it has been triggered. They represent the actual behavior or work the flow carries out. Filters do not describe behaviors inside a flow. Filters limit which records are included or displayed in lists and reports, but they do not run after a flow is triggered.
 Triggers do not represent behaviors after a flow starts. A trigger only defines the condition or event that starts a flow.
 Catalog Client Scripts do not represent behaviors that occur after a flow is triggered. They control client-side logic on catalog item forms.
questions.topic: Self Service & Automation - Workflow Studio

questions.question: Which items are mandatory when creating an email notification?
questions.explanation:
When to send must be defined when creating an email notification. It specifies the conditions or events that trigger the notification to be sent.
 What it will contain must be defined when creating an email notification. This includes the subject and message content that will be sent in the email.
 The email template does not need to be defined when creating an email notification. Email templates are optional formatting assets that can be applied to notifications but are not required to create one.
 An email digest does not need to be defined when creating an email notification. An email digest is used to combine multiple notifications into a single summary message and is configured separately from standard notifications.
questions.topic: Configuring Applications for Collaboration - Notifications

questions.question: Which field on a template record determines whether the template is ready for use?
questions.explanation:
The Active field determines whether a template is available for users to apply when creating new records. The Active field must be set to true for the template to be considered ready for use.
 The Short description field does not determine whether the template is ready for use. The short description field provides a brief explanation of the template's purpose.
 The User field does not determine whether the template is ready for use. The user field restricts template availability to a specific user.
 The Table field does not determine whether the template is ready for use. The table field specifies which table the template applies to.
questions.topic: Configuring Applications for Collaboration - Form templates and saving options

questions.question: Which application in ServiceNow is used to load data into the platform?
questions.explanation:
Import Sets is used to load data from different data sources and then maps that data into ServiceNow tables.
 The Configuration Management Database (CMDB) is not used to load external data. CMDB stores configuration item (CI) records rather than staging data for imports.
 Data Lookup Rules are not used to load external data. They adjust field values during form population or record creation, but they do not import or stage data.
 System update sets are not used to load external data. Update Sets capture configuration changes for migration between instances. They do not support importing data files or staging data for transforms.
questions.topic: Database Management and Platform Security - Importing Data

questions.question: Which component is part of the core architecture of a ServiceNow instance?
questions.explanation:
A load balancer is a core infrastructure component of a ServiceNow instance. It distributes incoming user requests across multiple application nodes to ensure high availability, reliability, and performance. By managing traffic efficiently, it helps prevent any single node from becoming overloaded and supports failover if a node becomes unavailable.
 A Management, Instrumentation, and Discovery (MID) Server is not part of the core cloud architecture of a ServiceNow instance. It is an optional, customer-installed agent that runs inside the organization's network to facilitate communication between the ServiceNow instance and on- premises systems, such as for Discovery, Orchestration, or IntegrationHub activities.
 An Update Set is an application-level mechanism used to capture and migrate configuration changes (such as customizations to forms, fields, or business rules) from one instance to another. It is not an infrastructure component, but rather a development and deployment tool within the ServiceNow platform.
 Service Portal is a configurable web interface framework used to create user-friendly front-end experiences for end users. While it runs on the ServiceNow platform, it is a feature or application layer capability rather than a core infrastructure component of the instance architecture.
questions.topic: Platform Overview and Navigation - The ServiceNow Instance

questions.question: Which area of responsibility is shared by all partners under the Shared Responsibility Model?
questions.explanation:
Compliance with regulatory and legal requirements is the only area shared by all partners in the Shared Responsibility Model. The matrix indicates that the customer, ServiceNow, the colocation facility, and the hyperscale cloud provider all hold responsibility in this domain. Each must ensure that their portion of the service stack, whether operational, infrastructural, or physical, meets regulatory expectations. Because all partners share accountability for compliance, this is the correct answer.
 Identity and access management is not shared by all partners. According to the responsibility matrix, only the customer is responsible for IAM. ServiceNow, the colocation facility, and the hyperscaler CSP do not participate in identity and access management activities. Because this responsibility is not distributed across all partners, it is not the correct answer.
 Monitoring and incident response are not shared by all partners. The matrix shows that both the customer and ServiceNow participate in incident management and logging/monitoring. Since not all partners share responsibility in this area, this choice is incorrect.
 Configuration and change management responsibilities fall primarily to the customer. The customer controls instance configuration, application settings, and customizations, while ServiceNow manages configuration of the platform features it provides. The hyperscale cloud provider and colocation facility do not participate in these configuration activities. Since responsibilities in this area do not extend equally across all partners, it is not universally shared.
questions.topic: Database Management and Platform Security - Shared Responsibility Model

questions.question: Which interface offers a guided experience to users as they create a Record Producer and another catalog item?
questions.explanation:
Catalog Builder provides a guided, visual experience for creating catalog items, record producers, and service request components. Catalog Builder explicitly supports delegated catalog creation, enabling non-technical users to build catalog items based on administrator-defined templates. It is designed to streamline catalog item creation through structured templates, variable configuration, and controlled publishing workflows.
 They should not use the Knowledge Homepage. The Knowledge Homepage is designed exclusively for viewing, browsing, and searching published knowledge articles, best practices, and troubleshooting content. It serves as an information repository rather than a tool for building catalog items or service request components.
 They should not use the Employee Center. Employee Center functions as a unified employee portal where users access services, tasks, knowledge, and organizational resources. It is as an experience layer for consumption, not a builder or design environment for catalog items.
 They should not use the Flow Designer. Flow Designer is designed to build automated workflows, logic, integrations, and process automation through no-code/low-code actions. It is as an automation engine rather than a catalog-authoring tool.
questions.topic: Self Service & Automation - Service Catalog

questions.question: Which fields are inherited by tables that extend from the Task table?
questions.explanation:
The State field is inherited by tables that extend from the Task table. It is used to track the lifecycle and progress of a task.
 The Work notes field is inherited by tables that extend from the Task table. It is used for internal updates and activity history on a task.
 The Knowledge base field is not inherited from the Task table. Knowledge base is used on Knowledge article records to identify where the article is stored.
 The Workflow field is not inherited from the Task table. Workflow is used on Knowledge article records to track article publishing and approval processes.
questions.topic: Configuring Applications for Collaboration - Task Management

questions.question: In which table do users create auto-generated follow-up entries for tasks or records they need to return to later?
questions.explanation:
Reminder is the table that allows users to create personal follow-up entries so they can remember tasks or records they need to return to later.
 My Work is not the table for creating follow-up entries. My Work displays tasks assigned to the user.
 Task Service Level Agreement (SLA) is not the table for creating follow-up entries. Task SLA tracks Service Level Agreements associated with a task.
 Incident is not the table for creating follow-up entries. Incident is a task-based table used to record and manage incidents reported by users.
questions.topic: Configuring Applications for Collaboration - Task Management

questions.question: Which ACL operation allows users to insert new records into a table?
questions.explanation:
The Create Access Control List (ACL) operation allows users to insert new records because it grants permission to add records to a table. Without Create permission, a user cannot submit new entries.
 The Read ACL operation does not allow inserting records because it only controls whether a user can view records in the table. Creating new records requires the Create operation.
 The Write ACL operation does not allow inserting new records because it controls the ability to update existing records. A user must have the Create operation to add new records to a table.
 The Delete ACL operation does not allow inserting records because it governs the ability to remove existing records from a table. It does not provide permissions to add new ones.
questions.topic: Database Management and Platform Security - Application/Access Control

questions.question: When importing data, what does coalesce a field mean?
options: The field determines if the transform updates a record or inserts a new one
The field is set to read-only so users cannot modify its value
The field is encrypted before being written to the staging table
The field is auto-mapped to the target table during the transform
questions.explanation:
Coalesce a field means the transform map uses that field to decide whether an incoming import set row updates an existing record in the target table or creates a new one. When a field is marked as coalesce, ServiceNow compares the incoming value with existing records; if it finds a match, the system updates that record, and if it finds no match, it inserts a new one. This mechanism is central to import reconciliation and prevents data duplication by ensuring that unique identifiers, such as serial numbers, email addresses, or other distinctive attributes, serve as the basis for record matching.
 Coalesce a field does not mean the system encrypts the field before writing it to the staging table. Coalescing plays no role in encryption and does not affect how data is protected in the staging or target tables. Encryption in ServiceNow operates through dedicated mechanisms such as column-level encryption, which administrators configure in the dictionary and manage through encryption contexts and key management. These controls function independently of transform map logic, so marking a field as coalesce does not trigger encryption or influence how encrypted values are created, processed, or stored.
 Coalesce a field does not mean the system auto-maps the field to the target table during a transform. Auto-mapping is a separate import set feature that attempts to match source and target fields based on name similarities. This automated mapping has no connection to the system's decision to update or insert records. Selecting a field as coalesce only instructs the transform map to use that field's value to identify existing records.
 Coalesce a field does not mean the system sets the field to read-only. Read-only behavior is controlled through dictionary attributes, such as read_only, UI policies, client scripts, or ACLs; none of which interact with or depend on coalesce settings in a transform map. Although coalesce influences data reconciliation during imports, it does not affect form behavior, field accessibility, or how users view or edit data.
questions.topic: Database Management and Platform Security - Importing Data

questions.question: What provides a single place to view multiple reports and visualizations together?
questions.explanation:
A dashboard provides a single place to view multiple reports and visualizations together. Dashboards allow users to monitor key metrics and insights in one consolidated view.
 A table does not provide a single place to view multiple reports and visualizations together. A table stores and organizes records and fields that hold the underlying data used in reports and visualizations.
 A form does not provide a single place to view multiple reports and visualizations together. A form displays a single record from a table so users can view or update its field values.
 A workspace does not provide a place to view multiple reports and visualizations together. A workspace is a modern interface that agents use to work with records, tasks, and related data.
questions.topic: Configuring Applications for Collaboration - Visualizations, Dashboards, and Platform Analytics

questions.question: What determines the sequence in which notifications are evaluated and sent when multiple notifications meet the same conditions?
questions.explanation:
Weight determines the sequence in which notifications are evaluated and sent when multiple notifications meet the same conditions. Notifications with a higher weight are processed first.
 Notification conditions do not determine the sequence in which notifications are evaluated and sent. Notification conditions define the event or record state that triggers the notification.
 An email template does not determine the sequence in which notifications are evaluated and sent. Email templates are used to format the content and layout of notification messages.
 Subscription does not determine the sequence in which notifications are evaluated and sent. Subscriptions allow users to opt in to receive notifications based on selected activity or preferences.
questions.topic: Configuring Applications for Collaboration - Notifications

questions.question: What are types of Visual Task Boards?
questions.explanation:
Freeform Board is a valid Visual Task Board type that allows users to manually create and manage task cards that are not tied to a list filter.
 Guided Board is a valid Visual Task Board type that organizes cards into lanes based on a defined field to support structured workflow transitions.
 Pivot table is not a Visual Task Board type. A Pivot Table aggregates data from a table into rows and columns to summarize records.
 Column is not a Visual Task Board type. Column is a data visualization type used in reports to compare values across categories using vertical bars.
questions.topic: Configuring Applications for Collaboration - Visual Task Boards (VTBs)

questions.question: Which features does an Administrator use to visualize Cl connections?
questions.explanation:
The Administrator uses Dependency Views to visualize configuration item (CI) relationships. This feature generates dynamic and interactive maps that represent how configuration items depend on, influence, or impact one another across services and infrastructure. It allows administrators to trace upstream and downstream dependencies, analyze potential service impacts, and understand relationship paths through an intuitive graphical interface designed specifically for Configuration Management Database (CMDB) relationship visualization.
 The Administrator uses Relationship Editor to visualize and modify Cl relationships. This tool provides a structured interface for viewing the existing relationship links between configuration items and for creating, editing, or removing these connections directly. It supports clear inspection of each Cl's relationship network and enables administrators to manage dependencies at record level without needing advanced mapping tools.
 The Administrator does not use CI Class Manager to visualize Cl relationships. This tool focuses solely on viewing and managing CMDB class schemas, inheritance models, class attributes, and hierarchy structures rather than relationship data between individual Cl records. Although it shows how classes relate conceptually, it does not provide a graphical or record-level view of actual Cl dependencies.
 The Administrator does not use CMDB Query Builder to visualize Cl relationships. While CMDB Query Builder enables users to construct, run, and analyze complex relationship-based queries across the CMDB, it is designed for data retrieval and reporting rather than graphical mapping. It displays relationship information as query results instead of interactive dependency maps, making it unsuitable for visual Cl relationship analysis.
 The Administrator does not use Mapping Assist Utility to visualize Cl relationships. This tool is intended to simplify field mapping during import set transformation using drag-and-drop assistance. It plays a role in data ingestion workflows but has no functionality related to exploring, viewing, or managing relationships between configuration items in the CMDB.
questions.topic: Database Management and Platform Security - CMDB and CSDM

questions.question: Which statement describes the function of the Application Navigator?
options: Displaying the main interface where records and lists appear for the selected module
Allowing a user to impersonate another user for testing
Providing access to all applications and modules a user is permitted to use
Capturing and displaying fields for individual records within a table
questions.explanation:
The function of the Application Navigator is to provide access to all applications and modules a user is permitted to use. The Application Navigator lists all applications and modules available to the logged-in user. It allows users to browse, filter, and favorite navigation items, and serves as the main entry point to features and records in the platform.
 Displaying the main interface where records and lists appear for the selected module is not a functionality of the Application Navigator. This is actually describing the content frame. The content frame is the main area of the interface where forms, lists, and pages are displayed.
 Allowing a user to impersonate another user for testing is not a functionality of the Application Navigator. This is actually describing the user impersonation. User impersonation is a separate function accessible through the user menu in the banner. It is not part of the Application Navigator's functionality.
 Capturing and displaying fields for individual records within a table is not a functionality of the Application Navigator. This is actually describing a form. A form is used to view and edit the fields of a single record in a table. It also appears in the content frame and not in the Application Navigator.
questions.topic: Platform Overview and Navigation - Platform capabilities and services

questions.question: What happens when an Administrator sets the default set field to true on an update set?
options: All other update sets in the same scope are set to default set = false
The update set becomes active across all application scopes
The update set becomes the default for its scope
All other update sets in the same scope are set to default set = true
Multiple default update sets are created for the same scope
questions.explanation:
Setting the default set to true makes the update set the default update set for its application scope.Any new configuration changes made in that scope are automatically captured in this update set.
 When the default set is set to true, the system automatically sets default set = false on all other update sets in the same scope to ensure only one default exists. When a new update set is marked as default, the platform automatically removes the default designation from any other update set in that same scope.
 Setting the default set to true does not affect other application scopes. Default update sets apply only within the selected scope. Default update sets are managed independently within each scope, so changes to the default designation apply only to update sets in the current scope.
 The system does not set multiple update sets to default set = true. Only one default update set is allowed per scope so the default set = false. When one update set is marked as default, all other update sets in that scope automatically have default set = false to maintain a single active default.
 Multiple default update sets are not allowed within the same scope. The system enforces a single default update set per scope to ensure configuration changes are captured consistently in only one active update set per scope.
questions.topic: Data Migration and Integration - System update sets

questions.question: What allows different versions of a form layout to be displayed to users based on conditions such as role or table values?
questions.explanation:
A view allows different versions of a form layout to be displayed to users based on conditions such as role or table values. This enables multiple layouts for the same record.
 A related list does not control which version of a form layout is displayed. Related Lists show records that have a relationship to the current record.
 A UI policy does not control which version of a form layout is displayed. UI Policies dynamically change field behavior such as making fields read- only, hidden, or mandatory.
 Dictionary Overrides do not control which version of a form layout is displayed. Dictionary Overrides change the behavior of inherited fields on child tables.
questions.topic: Configuring Applications for Collaboration - Task Management

questions.question: What does an Administrator do if a plugin does not appear in the Application Manager?
options: Create an update set to download the plugin
Request the plugin activation through Now Support
Activate the plugin from the Plugins module
questions.explanation:
An Administrator should request activation for the plugin through Now Support if it does not appear in the Application Manager. ServiceNow personnel process these requests to make the plugin available on the specified instance.
 Activating a plugin from the Plugins module does not resolve the issue if the plugin is not available in the instance. Plugins that are not available cannot be activated by an administrator, only be making a request through Now Support.
 Creating an update set does not activate or make a plugin available. Update sets are used to move configuration changes between instances, not to enable plugins.
 Cloning the instance does not make an unavailable plugin appear. Cloning is used to copy data and configuration from one instance to another, not to enable or activate plugins.
questions.topic: Instance Configuration - Installing applications and plugins

questions.question: Which field causes a UI Policy to execute the opposite of its defined actions when the condition is not met?
questions.explanation:
The reverse if false field causes a UI Policy to execute the opposite of its defined actions when the condition is not met. Reverse if false allows field behavior to be restored when the policy condition evaluates to false.
 The Execute if true field does not control whether opposite actions are executed. This option determines whether the UI Policy runs when the condition evaluates to true, but it does not reverse the configured actions.
 The Execute if false field does not cause opposite actions to run. This option allows the UI Policy to execute when the condition evaluates to false, but it does not automatically reverse previously applied actions.
 The Run scripts field does not control whether opposite actions are executed. This option enables the use of advanced scripting within the UI Policy but does not affect the reversal of configured UI Policy actions.
questions.topic: Data Migration and Integration - UI Policies

questions.question: What are types of Service Catalog items?
questions.explanation:
A record producer is a type of catalog item that allows users to create records in a table through a simplified, user-friendly form.
 An order guide is a type of catalog item that helps users order multiple related items in a single request.
 A variable set is not a type of catalog item. Variable sets are reusable groups of variables that help structure the form used within catalog items.
 A Catalog client script is not a type of catalog item. Catalog client scripts are used to control client-side behavior within a catalog form.
questions.topic: Self Service & Automation - Service Catalog

questions.question: Where do users navigate when they need to order new laptop?
questions.explanation:
The Service Catalog is where users go to order items like laptops, monitors, and other requestable services. It presents available catalog items and guides users through submitting a request for what they need.
 Navigating to the Knowledge Base does not allow users to order a laptop. The Knowledge Base is where users read articles to find information and troubleshoot issues.
 Navigating to Flow Designer does not allow users to order a laptop. Flow Designer is a tool used to build automated workflows and logic without scripting.
 Navigating to the Configuration Management Database (CMDB) Workspace does not allow users to order a laptop. The CMDB Workspace manages configuration items and visualizing relationships within the CMDB.
questions.topic: Self Service & Automation - Service Catalog

questions.question: Which role is required to create or modify Access Control rules?
questions.explanation:
The Security Administrator [security_admin] role is required to create or modify Access Control rules because Access Control List (ACL) changes are considered high-security operations. A user must elevate to security_admin before creating, editing, or deleting ACL records.
 The Administrator [admin] role alone cannot create or modify ACLs. ACL changes require elevation to the security_admin role. Administrators must explicitly elevate privileges before editing ACLs.
 The ITIL [itil] role cannot create or modify ACLs. The Information Technology Infrastructure Library (ITIL) role is intended for users who fulfill tasks and manage records, not for configuring platform-level security.
 The snc_internal role cannot create or modify ACLs. This is a system role used for internal platform operations, not for defining or managing ACLs.
questions.topic: Database Management and Platform Security - Application/Access Control

questions.question: Which use case is best suited for a business rule?
options: Modifying the options in a choice list based on a user's role
Making a field mandatory based on another field value
Enforcing data validation at the database level
Dynamically making a field read-only based on another field
questions.explanation:
Enforcing data validation at the database level is best suited for a business rule. Business rules run on the server and apply regardless of how a record is created or updated.
 Dynamically making a field read-only is not best suited for a business rule. UI Policies dynamically control read-only, visible, and mandatory behaviors on form fields.
 Modifying choice list options based on a user's role is not best suited for a business rule. Client scripts are used to dynamically control available choice values on a form at runtime.
 Making a field mandatory based on another field value is not best suited for a business rule. UI Policies are used to dynamically enforce mandatory, visible, and read-only behaviors on form fields.
questions.topic: Data Migration and Integration - Business Rules

questions.question: Which table stores the configuration change records that are used to move changes between instances?
questions.explanation:
The Customer Update [sys_update_xml] table stores the individual configuration change records captured within an update set. These records represent the actual changes, such as modified fields, scripts, UI policies, and other configuration elements that are transported between instances when an update set is moved.
 The Update Set [sys_update_set] table does not store the individual configuration change records that are moved between instances. It stores the update set header record, including details such as the name, state, and application scope, and serves as a logical container that groups captured changes together.
 The Scheduled Job [sysauto] table does not store update set records, as it is used to define and manage scheduled system jobs. Scheduled jobs are operational automation components unrelated to the tracking or movement of configuration changes between instances.
 The Dictionary Entries [sys_dictionary] table does not store update set records. This table contains metadata that defines table structures, field attributes, and schema information. While some dictionary changes may be captured in customer update records, the sys_dictionary table itself is not where update sets are stored.
questions.topic: Data Migration and Integration - System update sets

questions.question: Which feature enables a user to complete a form with predefined values?
questions.explanation:
Templates allow the quick population of a form with predefined field values. They help speed up data entry by automatically filling in commonly used values.
 Related Lists do not populate a form with predefined field values. Related Lists display records from other tables that are associated with the current record.
 Tags do not populate a form with predefined field values. Tags are used to label or categorize records so users can easily group or find them later. Favorites do not populate a form with predefined field values. Favorites allow users to bookmark frequently accessed lists, modules, or records for quick access.
questions.topic: Configuring Applications for Collaboration - Form templates and saving options

questions.question: Which data visualization types are allowed in reports or dashboards?
questions.explanation:
Pie is a valid data visualization type in reports or dashboards. It displays data as proportional slices of a circular chart to compare parts of a whole.
 Heatmap is a valid data visualization type that in reports or dashboards. It represents values using color intensity to highlight trends or concentration patterns.
 Guided Board is not a data visualization used in reports or dashboards. Guided Board is a type of Visual Task Board used to organize and track tasks in a guided workflow format.
 Freeform is not a data visualization used in reports or dashboards. Freeform is a type of Visual Task Board that allows users to manually arrange and manage tasks in a flexible layout.
questions.topic: Configuring Applications for Collaboration - Visualizations, Dashboards, and Platform Analytics

questions.question: Which capability offers employees an automated conversational experience to help them find answers and complete basic tasks?
questions.explanation:
Virtual Agent provides automated, conversational assistance that helps users find answers and complete basic tasks, which directly reduces simple support tickets.
 Notifications do not provide automated conversations for helping users complete tasks. Notifications are used to inform users of updates or changes through email, SMS, or in-platform alerts.
 A Record Producer does not provide guided, automated conversations for resolving support issues. Record Producers simply create task based records in a table through a simplified form in the Service Catalog.
 Connect Chat does not automate conversations to help users complete basic tasks. Connect Chat supports real-time messaging between users or support agents.
questions.topic: Self Service & Automation - Virtual Agent

questions.question: Which resource does an Administrator use as a blueprint to map IT Services?
questions.explanation:
The Administrator uses the Common Service Data Model (CSDM) as a blueprint to map IT Services. This model provides a standardized and structured framework for modeling and mapping IT services across the ServiceNow platform. CSDM acts as the blueprint that defines how service-related data should be organized, how IT services relate to applications and infrastructure, and how these relationships support ServiceNow products such as Service Mapping, Configuration Management Database (CMDB), and IT Operations Management (ITOM). By following the CSDM, administrators ensure consistent service modeling practices, better data quality, and a unified view of service dependencies that align with industry best practices.
 The Administrator does not use the Configuration Management Database (CMDB) as a blueprint to map IT Services. The CMDB is a repository that stores configuration items (CIs) and their relationships but does not provide a service modeling framework. While the CMDB supports service modeling by housing the underlying data, it does not define how services should be structured or mapped; instead, it relies on frameworks like CSDM to give meaning and organization to the stored configuration data.
 The Administrator does not use a data policy as a blueprint to map IT Services. Data policies are designed to enforce data quality rules and field- level consistency, not to define or structure IT services. Data policies help ensure correct data entry and maintain uniformity across forms and APIs, but they play no role in mapping IT services or modeling service relationships within the CMDB or service architecture.
 The Administrator does not use the Mapping Assist utility as a blueprint to map IT Services. This feature is intended to help create and automate field mappings in transform maps during data imports. Mapping Assist simplifies data integration tasks by suggesting or generating field correspondences, but it does not provide capabilities for defining service models, building service hierarchies, or creating a blueprint for IT service mapping.
questions.topic: Database Management and Platform Security - CMDB and CSDM

questions.question: What is a user allowed to do within the User menu of the Next Experience Unified Navigation?
questions.explanation:
Within the User menu of the Next Experience Unified Navigation, a user can update their user profile. Users can view and modify personal details. Within the User menu of the Next Experience Unified Navigation, a user can edit preferences. Users can adjust settings.
 Within the User menu of the Next Experience Unified Navigation, a user cannot change the application scope. This action is performed from Studio or Application Picker when developing or configuring applications.
 Within the User menu of the Next Experience Unified Navigation, a user cannot edit a favorite. Favorites are managed directly from the navigation bar where users can add, reorder, or remove favorite modules.
questions.topic: Instance Configuration - Common user interfaces in the Platform

questions.question: What displays comments, work notes, and record history on a form?
questions.explanation:
An activity stream displays comments, work notes, and record history on a form. Using an activity stream, users can review past activity on the record.
 Related lists do not display comments or record history. A related list displays records that have a relationship to the record shown on the form.
 Related links do not display comments or record history. Related links provide quick actions or navigation options associated with the current record.
 Fields do not display comments, work notes, or record history. A field is a data entry element used to capture a specific value on the form.
questions.topic: Configuring Applications for Collaboration - List and Form anatomy

questions.question: Which value is stored in the child task record when a parent-child relationship is created between tasks?
options: A task record reference stored in the Parent reference field
A record reference stored in a Document ID field
A user reference stored in a Reference field
Multiple records stored in a Glide list field
questions.explanation:
When a parent-child relationship is created, the child task stores a reference to the parent task in the Parent field.
 A user reference stored in a Reference field is not the value stored in the child task record to create a parent-child relationship. Reference fields store a link to a record on another table.
 Multiple records stored in a Glide list field are not the value stored in the child task record to create a parent-child relationship. Glide list fields store multiple related records.
 A record reference stored in a Document ID field is not the value stored in the child task record to create a parent-child relationship. Document ID fields store a reference to a record on any table in the instance.
questions.topic: Configuring Applications for Collaboration - Task Management

questions.question: What is the best practice for an Administrator who has marked an Update Set as Complete but needs to make additional changes?
options: Add changes to the default update set
Change the state back to In Progress
Create an entirely new update set
questions.explanation:
Creating a new update set is the best practice when additional changes are needed after an update set is marked Complete. Completed update sets are read-only and should not be modified.
 Changing the state of a completed update set back to In Progress is not recommended. Completed update sets are intended to remain read-only to preserve change history and integrity.
 Manually modifying Customer Updates [sys_update_xml] records is not a best practice. These records are system-generated and should not be edited directly.
 Adding changes to the default update set is not a best practice. The default update set should be avoided for intentional configuration changes.
questions.topic: Data Migration and Integration - System update sets

questions.question: What is automatically inherited from the Task table?
questions.explanation:
The system automatically inherits fields from the Task table. This includes standard Task fields such as Assigned To, Priority, and State.
 Business rules defined on the Task table execute automatically for tables that extend Task because business rules evaluate operations based on the table hierarchy. When a child table performs an operation that meets the rule conditions, the rule executes without requiring additional configuration.
 The system does not automatically inherit UI policies. UI policies apply to specific forms and field layouts, not table inheritance. A child table does not reuse the form configuration of its parent.
 The system does not automatically inherit views. Views are unique to the form.
 The system does not automatically inherit Related Links from the Task table. Related links are generated by UI Actions, client logic, or scripts that are defined on a specific table. A child table does not receive the Related Links of its parent table unless the underlying UI actions are explicitly configured for that table.
questions.topic: Database Management and Platform Security - Data Schema

questions.question: What lists the items and modules available in the instance?
questions.explanation:
The All menu lists all menu items and modules available in the instance. Users can navigate to all applications and modules from the All menu.
 The Favorites menu does not list all menu items and modules. The Favorites menu displays only items a user has saved for quick access. The Workspaces menu does not list all menu items and modules. The Workspaces menu provides access to role-based workspaces.
 The History menu does not list all menu items and modules. The History menu displays recently visited modules and records.
 Globe does not list all menu items and modules. Globe is the application scope indicator in ServiceNow, showing which application scope you are currently working in.
questions.topic: Platform Overview and Navigation - Next Experience Unified Navigation

questions.question: Which components are included in the list interface?
questions.explanation:
Fields are components of the list interface. They display the values stored in each record within a column.
 Columns are components of the list interface. They define which fields are displayed across all records in the list.
 Related lists are not components of the list interface. Related lists appear on forms and display records that are related to the current record. Sections are not components of the list interface. Sections organize fields on a form into collapsible groups.
 An activity stream is not a component of the list interface. Activity stream displays comments, work notes, and record history on a form.
questions.topic: Configuring Applications for Collaboration - List and Form anatomy

questions.question: In which order does ServiceNow evaluate ACL rules when determining access to a record and its fields?
options: ServiceNow evaluates table first, from most general to most specific, then field, from most general to most specific.
ServiceNow evaluates field first, from most specific to most general, then table, from most specific to most general.
ServiceNow evaluates table first, from most specific to most general, then field, from most specific to most general.
ServiceNow evaluates field first, from most general to most specific, then table, from most general to most specific.
questions.explanation: ServiceNow evaluates table first, from most specific to most general, then field, from most specific to most general. ServiceNow evaluates access control list (ACL) rules by first checking table-level ACLs, starting with the most specific match and progressing to more general ones. After all applicable table ACLs are evaluated, the system then evaluates field-level ACLs, also from most specific to most general. Access is granted only if every relevant ACL returns true, making this execution order essential to the platform's security model.
questions.topic: Database Management and Platform Security - Data Schema

questions.question: What happens when a user fails a field-level Read ACL?
options: The system displays a warning message asking the user if they want to continue.
The system logs a warning but still allows the user to view and update the field.
The system denies access to the entire record and prevents the user from viewing it.
The system hides the field and prevents the user from viewing its value.
questions.explanation:
The system hides the field and prevents the user from viewing its value. Failing a field access control rule (ACL) blocks access only to that specific field. The record remains accessible, but the restricted field is not displayed or returned to the user.
 The system does not deny access to the entire record and prevents the user from viewing it. This only happens when a table ACL fails, not a field ACL. A failed field ACL restricts a single field while still allowing access to the rest of the record.
 The system does not display a warning message asking the user if they want to continue. ACL failures do not generate user prompts. ACLs enforce access automatically without offering a bypass or confirmation option.
 The system does not log a warning and still allows the user to view and update the field. ACL failures do not permit access. When a field ACL fails, the system blocks the user from both reading and writing that field.
questions.topic: Database Management and Platform Security - Application/Access Control

questions.question: Which file formats are imported using Import Sets?
questions.explanation:
Import Sets support XML. XML is a structured data format that can be parsed and converted into Import Set rows for processing.
 Import Sets support CSV. CSV files are structured, delimited text files that can be imported into staging tables for transformation.
 Import Sets cannot load PDF files. PDF is not a structured data format that the system can convert into Import Set rows. PDF files cannot be parsed into staging tables.
 Import Sets cannot load image files (JPG/PNG). The system requires structured data formats for staging table creation.
 Import Sets cannot load ZIP files. Compressed archive files are not supported as direct structured data sources for Import Sets.
questions.topic: Database Management and Platform Security - Importing Data

questions.question: Which Security Center role grants create permission, read access to all records, and write access limited to the user's own entries?
questions.explanation:
Security Task Managers can work on Security Tasks assigned to them and can create and manage new tasks in Security Center. They can view tasks assigned to other users but cannot edit those tasks, and their access is restricted to task-manager-specific pages. This combination of task-creation ability, limited task-editing permissions, and broader visibility matches the capabilities described in the scenario.
 System Administrators can fully manage Security Tasks, including viewing, creating, assigning, and deleting them. This role has unrestricted access to task operations and is not limited in what tasks it can edit or manage. Because administrators possess complete task-management capabilities, this role does not match a scenario in which a user is restricted from editing tasks assigned to others.
 Security Center Viewers can view Security Tasks but cannot create, edit, or delete them. Their access to Security Tasks is strictly read-only, and they do not participate in task management or task execution. Since this role cannot perform any task-modification or task-creation actions, it does not align with responsibilities involving managing or working on tasks.
 ITIL users can interact with Security Tasks only when those tasks are assigned to them. They cannot view all Security Tasks across the system and do not have permissions to create or manage tasks for other users. Their task access is limited to their own assigned work, which does not align with roles that require viewing or managing tasks outside their assignment.
questions.topic: Database Management and Platform Security - Security Center

questions.question: What is used to store JavaScript that runs on the server?
questions.explanation:
Script Includes are used to store JavaScript that runs on the server. Script Includes contain reusable server-side logic that can be called from other scripts.
 Client Scripts are not used to store JavaScript that runs on the server. Client Scripts control form behavior during user interaction in the browser.
 UI Actions are not used to store JavaScript that runs on the server. UI Actions define user-triggered actions and may run client-side or server- side, but they are not intended for shared logic.
 UI Scripts are not used to store JavaScript that runs on the server. UI Scripts store client-side JavaScript that runs in the user's browser.
questions.topic: Data Migration and Integration - Scripting in ServiceNow

questions.question: What does the Administrator use to add custom modules to the Application Navigator?
questions.explanation:
The Application Menu module allows Administrators to add custom modules to the Application Navigator. It defines the application structure and controls which modules appear within it.
 The Dictionary module does not allow Administrators to add custom modules. The Dictionary module is used to manage field definitions, table schema, and field attributes.
 Data policies do not allow Administrators to add custom modules. Data policies enforce field requirements and data consistency during data entry.
 The Application Registry module does not allow Administrators to add custom modules. The Application Registry module is used to configure OAuth settings and register applications for integration.
questions.topic: Instance Configuration - Personalizing/customizing the instance

questions.question: Which interface displays multiple records from a table in rows and columns?
questions.explanation:
A list displays multiple records from a table in rows and columns. Users can sort, filter, and edit records directly from a list.
 Global Search does not display multiple records from a table in rows and columns. Global Search allows users to search across multiple tables and records throughout the platform.
 History does not display multiple records from a table in rows and columns. History allows users to return to recently viewed records, lists, or modules.
 A form does not display multiple records from a table in rows and columns. A form displays a single record from a table so users can view or update its field values.
questions.topic: Configuring Applications for Collaboration - Lists, Filters, and Tags

questions.question: Which feature dynamically makes a field mandatory on a form when a specific condition is met?
questions.explanation:
UI Policy Actions set the actual field behavior; mandatory, read-only, or visible. They execute only when the parent UI Policy's conditions evaluate to true; they do not decide when the behavior applies. In practice, the dynamic change to mandatory is enforced by the action, while the timing is driven by the policy conditions that trigger those actions.
 UI Policy conditions control when a UI Policy is applied on a form. The policy conditions evaluate field values client-side to determine whether specific UI behaviors, such as making a field mandatory, should run. UI Policies are explicitly configured by defining conditions that match field values and then adding UI Policy Actions that enforce behaviors like mandatory, read-only, or visible attributes.
 On Load is a client-side script type that runs once when the form first renders; it initializes values or layout before the user interacts with the form, but it does not continuously evaluate changing conditions after load, so it is not the feature that toggles a field to mandatory in response to later user actions.
 Run scripts is an advanced option on a UI Policy that executes client-side logic when the policy condition is true or false; it extends behavior for complex cases, but it does not directly set field attributes, so making a field mandatory still relies on the UI Policy's actions rather than the script itself.
questions.topic: Data Migration and Integration - UI Policies

questions.question: What are valid states of an update set?
questions.explanation:
The Complete state indicates that an update set is finished and no longer captures changes. Completed update sets are ready to be moved to another instance.
 The Ignore state indicates that an update set or individual update should not be applied. Ignored updates are skipped during the commit process.
 The Draft state is not a valid update set state. Draft is a publication state used for knowledge articles.
 The Published state is not a valid update set state. Published is a publication state used for knowledge articles.
questions.topic: Data Migration and Integration - System update sets

questions.question: What are variable types in the Service Catalog?
questions.explanation:
Date is a Service Catalog variable type used to capture a calendar date.
 Select Box is a Service Catalog variable type that allows users to pick from a predefined list of options.
 A String is not a Service Catalog variable type. It is a basic text field used in lists and forms.
 A Choice is not a Service Catalog variable type. It is a field type that allows users to select from a predefined set of values.
questions.topic: Self Service & Automation - Service Catalog

questions.question: Which events occur on the client side?
options: When a database record is accessed
questions.explanation:
Form loading occurs on the client side. onLoad client scripts execute in the user's browser when a form is first displayed. ServiceNow defines onLoad as a client-side script type that runs as soon as the form loads, before the user interacts with it.
 Form submission also occurs on the client side. onSubmit client scripts run in the user's browser when the user submits a form, allowing the system to validate or stop the submission before data is sent to the server.
 Database records being accessed does not occur on the client side. Database operations, including reading, querying, and loading records, are executed server-side by Business Rules and other server-side scripts, not by the browser.
 Table data being modified does not occur on the client side. Table updates and database writes occur on the server using server-side logic, not on the client. Client-side scripts cannot modify database tables directly.
questions.topic: Data Migration and Integration - Scripting in ServiceNow

questions.question: Which field behaviors are controlled using a UI Policy?
questions.explanation:
The mandatory behavior of a field can be controlled using a UI Policy. UI Policies can require users to enter a value before saving a record.
 The read-only behavior of a field can be controlled using a UI Policy. UI Policies can prevent users from editing a field on a form.
 The encrypted behavior of a field can not be controlled by a UI Policy. Encryption is defined at the dictionary level.
 The audited behavior of a field can not be controlled by a UI Policy. Auditing tracks changes to field values.
questions.topic: Data Migration and Integration - UI Policies

questions.question: Who is responsible for backup and restoration under the Shared Responsibility Model in ServiceNow?
questions.explanation:
In the Shared Responsibility Model, the ServiceNow team is responsible for performing platform-level backup and restoration tasks as part of its operational and infrastructure management duties. This includes maintaining reliable backup processes, ensuring recoverability, and safeguarding customer data within the managed ServiceNow environment so that customers benefit from a secure and resilient platform without needing to handle these technical operations themselves.
 In the Shared Responsibility Model, the customer is responsible for data quality, data governance, and proper configuration within the instance, but they do not manage any of the platform's underlying backup or restoration operations. Their responsibilities focus on how data is entered, maintained, and used; not on the technical mechanisms that protect or restore the platform's data.
 In the Shared Responsibility Model, the colocation facility provides and maintains the physical hosting environment, including power, cooling, and building security, but it has no involvement in performing platform data backup or restoration tasks. Its role is strictly limited to the physical infrastructure layer, far removed from the application-level processes that handle customer data protection.
 In the Shared Responsibility Model, the cloud service provider maintains and secures the underlying cloud infrastructure that supports the ServiceNow platform, but it does not perform ServiceNow-specific application backup or restoration. While it ensures infrastructure availability and robustness, it does not manage the platform's operational data protection processes, which remain the responsibility of ServiceNow.
questions.topic: Database Management and Platform Security - Shared Responsibility Model

questions.question: Which interface displays one record from a table?
questions.explanation:
A form displays one record from a table. It allows users to view and edit the fields and details of a single record.
 A dashboard does not display one record from a table. A dashboard shows visualizations such as reports and widgets for monitoring data.
 A report does not display one record from a table. A report presents aggregated data using charts, lists, and visual summaries.
 A workspace does not display one record from a table. A workspace provides a modern interface that centralizes tasks, records, and tools for agents.
questions.topic: Instance Configuration - Common user interfaces in the Platform

questions.question: What are ServiceNow core actions in Flow Designer?
questions.explanation:
The Ask for Approval action is a ServiceNow core action that is used to initiate approval requests directly within Flow Designer, allowing approvals to be automated as part of a workflow.
 The Create Record action is a ServiceNow core action that is used to generate new records such as Catalog Tasks or other table entries within a Flow Designer process.
 The Send Reports action is not a ServiceNow core action because Flow Designer cannot send or schedule reports; reporting capabilities are handled through the platform's Reports and Dashboards features, not through Flow Designer.
 The Create Event action is not a ServiceNow core action because Flow Designer does not generate platform events; events are raised through system logging mechanisms or server-side scripts, not through core Flow Designer actions.
 The Send Notification action is not a ServiceNow core action because notifications are sent through the platform's Notification framework or custom spokes rather than through Flow Designer's core action set.
questions.topic: Self Service & Automation - Workflow Studio

questions.question: When running a transform, how does an Administrator force the system to create a new record for every import set row?
options: Ensure no coalesce field is selected
questions.explanation:
An Administrator ensures that every import set row becomes a new record by selecting no coalesce field. This approach gives the system no criteria to match against existing target records.
 An Administrator does not use single-field coalesce. This approach allows the transform to update an existing target record when the field value matches, preventing every import set row from being inserted as a new record.
 An Administrator does not use multiple-field coalesce. This approach provides broader matching criteria, allowing the system to update an existing record when all coalesce field values match, rather than inserting a new one.
 An Administrator does not use a conditional coalesce script. This still enables the system to evaluate matching criteria during transformation, allowing updates to existing records instead of forcing all rows to be inserted as new ones.
questions.topic: Database Management and Platform Security - Importing Data

questions.question: Which options are states in the knowledge article lifecycle?
questions.explanation:
Draft is the initial state the knowledge article enters after it is submitted.
 Retired is a state in the knowledge article lifecycle. Retired means the article has been removed from active use but is still stored in the system.
 Archive is not a state in the knowledge article lifecycle. The state where the functionality of removing an article from being available for use from an end user is called Retired.
 Test is not a state in the knowledge article lifecycle. Test is used in Flow Designer to ensure a flow is working as designed.
 Preview is not a state in the knowledge article lifecycle. A preview allows a user to see components like a form or new service catalog item before it is saved.
questions.topic: Self Service & Automation - Knowledge Management

questions.question: Who is responsible for the data within a ServiceNow instance under the Shared Responsibility Model?
questions.explanation:
In the Shared Responsibility Model, the customer is responsible for the data within a ServiceNow instance, including its accuracy, classification, governance, retention, access permissions, and protection against loss or unauthorized disclosure; the customer determines what data to store, how it is labeled and restricted, who can access it, and how it is ingested and maintained across integrations and business processes, because ServiceNow's role covers the platform and underlying services while data stewardship and compliance for content remain the customer's duty.
 In the Shared Responsibility Model, ServiceNow is responsible for the SaaS platform and underlying system; covering areas such as platform availability, infrastructure security, patching, and baseline controls, but it does not own, manage, or govern the customer's data content; customers must ensure their instance data is correct, properly classified, and protected in line with their organizational and regulatory requirements.
 In the Shared Responsibility Model, the colocation facility provides the physical hosting environment such as building security, power, cooling, and physical access controls for hardware but does not manage, control, classify, or protect application-level customer data stored within a ServiceNow instance; data stewardship remains outside the remit of a colocation provider.
 In the Shared Responsibility Model, the cloud service provider operates and secures the cloud infrastructure components that run the SaaS platform, but it does not assume responsibility for customer-entered data within ServiceNow; the governance, classification, and protection of that data remain the customer's responsibility.
questions.topic: Database Management and Platform Security - Shared Responsibility Model

questions.question: What do users use to interact with Virtual Agent?
questions.explanation:
End users interact with Virtual Agent via Microsoft Teams. Microsoft Teams is a supported channel for Virtual Agent conversations. It allows users to interact with Virtual Agent through the Teams chat interface.
 End users interact with Virtual Agent via Slack. Slack is a supported channel for Virtual Agent conversations. It enables users to engage with Virtual Agent in real time using the Slack messaging app.
 Google Chat is not a supported channel for Virtual Agent conversations. Google Chat is integrated through a Flow Designer spoke to manage messages, spaces, and communications.
 Connect Chat is not a supported channel for Virtual Agent conversations. Connect Chat provides real-time chat capabilities for user-to-user communication within the platform.
questions.topic: Self Service & Automation - Virtual Agent

questions.question: Which domain layer of the CSDM contains customer-facing service offerings that users can request or subscribe to?
questions.explanation:
The Consume domain represents customer-facing services and service offerings that users can request or subscribe to.
 The Foundation domain contains core Configuration Management Database (CMDB) elements such as locations, groups, and users; it does not represent customer-facing offerings.
 The Build domain includes technical services and deployment components used to support applications, not the services consumed by end users.
 The Design domain contains application and service design elements, including logical models and architectural components, rather than user- facing offerings.
questions.topic: Database Management and Platform Security - CMDB and CSDM

questions.question: Which capability helps Virtual Agent understand user intent through natural language?
questions.explanation:
