Natural Language Understanding (NLU) models help Virtual Agent understand user intent and interpret natural language input. They enable Virtual Agent to recognize what the user is asking and respond appropriately.
 UI Policies do not help Virtual Agent understand natural language. UI Policies control client-side form behavior such as making fields visible, mandatory, or read-only.
 Localization does not help Virtual Agent understand natural language. Localization is used to translate and adapt platform text for different languages and regions.
 Flows does not help Virtual Agent understand natural language. Flows are automated sequences built in Flow Designer to perform actions and process logic.
questions.topic: Self Service & Automation - Virtual Agent

questions.question: Who is responsible for the platform infrastructure under the Shared Responsibility Model?
questions.explanation:
In the Shared Responsibility Model, the ServiceNow is responsible for the platform infrastructure and the security of the underlying system, which covers the SaaS platform's compute, storage, networking, availability, patching, and baseline security controls, while the customer retains responsibility for what they put into the instance, i.e. their data, including how it is classified, governed, and protected.
 In the Shared Responsibility Model, the colocation facility is responsible for the physical hosting environment such as building security, power, cooling, and physical access controls, but does not operate or secure the platform infrastructure itself.
 In the Shared Responsibility Model, the cloud service provider operates and secures cloud infrastructure components that host the SaaS environment such as hypervisors, storage subsystems, and network fabric, but it does not assume responsibility for the platform infrastructure decisions or controls at the application/platform layer, nor for any customer-entered data.
 In the Shared Responsibility Model, the customer is not responsible for the platform infrastructure; instead, they are accountable for their instance data; its accuracy, classification, governance, and protection, ensuring their content aligns with organizational policies and regulatory obligations while leveraging controls provided by the platform.
questions.topic: Database Management and Platform Security - Shared Responsibility Model

questions.question: Which module displays a visual representation of table inheritance?
questions.explanation:
The Schema Map displays a visual representation of table inheritance by providing a graphical view of parent and child table relationships. It also shows extended fields and dictionary structures, making it useful for understanding how tables relate to one another.
 The Localization Framework does not display a visual representation of table inheritance. The Localization Framework is used for translating UI text and managing localized content. It provides translation capabilities, not hierarchical table diagrams.
 A Transform Map does not display a visual representation of table inheritance. A Transform Map defines how data is mapped from an import set to a target table. It supports data loading operations.
 The configuration item (CI) Class Manager does not display a visual representation of table inheritance. The CI Class Manager is used to visualize and manage the Configuration Management Database (CMDB) class hierarchy inheritance specifically, rather than general application table inheritance.
questions.topic: Database Management and Platform Security - Data Schema

questions.question: What can a user create for items they access often and want to return to quickly?
questions.explanation:
A user can create a favorite to allow them to navigate quickly to items that they use often.
 A user cannot create a dashboard to navigate quickly to items they use often. A dashboard is used to display a collection of widgets to analyze data.
 A user cannot create a filter to navigate quickly to items they use often. A filter allows the user to reduce the amount of records being shown based on defined conditions.
 A user cannot create a tag to navigate quickly to items they use often. A tag is a collection of key words to identify records.
questions.topic: Instance Configuration - Personalizing/customizing the instance

questions.question: What is the purpose of Customer Actions in Security Center?
options: Address security risks that remain unresolved after an upgrade
Create Security Tasks that remain unresolved after an upgrade
Review customizations that may require backout after an upgrade
Log fixes that the system applies automatically
questions.explanation:
The purpose of Customer Actions in Security Center is to help administrators address security risks that remain unresolved after an upgrade. The platform cannot automatically apply certain fixes without risking disruption to custom configurations. Customer Actions highlights these items so that administrators can manually review and apply the required remediations in a controlled manner, ensuring their instance remains secure while preserving any customizations that could otherwise be overwritten or broken by automated updates.
 The purpose of Customer Actions in Security Center is not to create unresolved Security Tasks after an upgrade. Security Tasks are customer-created items used to monitor, prioritize, and manage security-related work in one central place, but they are not generated automatically through upgrades. Customer Actions focuses on upgrade-related risks requiring customer attention, not on generating tasks on behalf of the system.
 The purpose of Customer Actions in Security Center is not to evaluate or review customizations that might need to be backed out after an upgrade. Customizations are tracked through update sets, which provide their own dedicated backout mechanism. Customer Actions is instead centered on identifying unresolved security risks; not analyzing configuration changes or determining whether a customization should be reverted.
 The purpose of Customer Actions in Security Center is not to log automatically applied fixes. ServiceNow does not automatically implement certain security-related changes because doing so could conflict with or break existing custom configurations. Instead, Customer Actions provides clear, step-by-step guidance so administrators can apply the necessary fixes themselves in a safe and controlled manner.
questions.topic: Database Management and Platform Security - Security Center

questions.question: Where are UI Policies evaluated when a user interacts with a form?
questions.explanation:
UI Policies are evaluated on the client side when a user interacts with a form. UI Policies control form behavior in real time as the user views or edits a record.
 UI Policies are not evaluated server side. Server-side processing occurs after data is submitted, such as through Business Rules or Flows.
 The Global scope does not determine where UI Policies are evaluated. Global scope controls application availability and access, not form behavior.
 The System Log does not determine where UI Policies are evaluated. The System Log records system events, errors, and warnings for troubleshooting purposes.
questions.topic: Data Migration and Integration - UI Policies

questions.question: Which roles manage multiple Knowledge Bases?
questions.explanation:
The Knowledge administrator [knowledge_admin] role can manage multiple knowledge bases because it is specifically designed for administering Knowledge Management and modifying knowledge bases.
 The Administrator role [admin] can manage multiple knowledge bases. It has full platform access and can configure all knowledge management settings.
 The ITIL role does not allow users to manage multiple knowledge bases. This role is primarily for incident and request fulfillment work.
 The Catalog manager [catalog_manager] role does not allow users to manage multiple knowledge bases. This role is primarily for maintaining service catalog items and categories.
questions.topic: Self Service & Automation - Knowledge Management

questions.question: Which statement is true about moving a task card from one lane to another?
options: A field value on the underlying task record is updated.
All fields have to be completed before moving.
A user has to have an admin role to move a card.
questions.explanation:
When a user moves a task card to a different lane, the field that the lanes are based on is updated on the underlying task record to match the new lane value.
 The move can indeed be cancelled. Users can reverse a move by dragging the card back to the previous lane or pressing escape during the move.
 All fields do not need to be completed before moving. Only mandatory fields are required to be completed when a task is going through a lane change.
 An admin role is not needed to move a card. Users can move cards as long as they have permission to update the underlying task record.
questions.topic: Configuring Applications for Collaboration - Visual Task Boards (VTBs)

questions.question: What does a System Administrator create to make the Assigned to field on a form mandatory when the State field is set to Resolved?
questions.explanation:
The System Administrator uses a UI policy to make the Assigned to field mandatory when the State is set to Resolved. They can create a UI policy to dynamically modify a form behavior based on conditions.
 The System Administrator can create a data policy to enforce rules at the server level, but a data policy does not control real-time form behavior.
 The System Administrator can create a business rule to run server-side logic, but a business rule cannot dynamically change form behavior.
 The System Administrator can create a security rule to control access to data, but a security rule cannot modify form behavior or apply conditional field requirements.
questions.topic: Data Migration and Integration - UI Policies

questions.question: Which statement best describes an Update Set?
options: A collection of configuration changes that can be moved between instances
Protection for applications by identifying and restricting access to application files and data
A collection of field mappings that define relationships between import set fields and fields in a target table
A collection of team members based on specific requirements
questions.explanation:
An update set is a group of configuration changes that can be moved from one instance to another. This allows administrators to promote configuration between environments.
 An update set is not a set of team members defined to meet specific requirements. This description corresponds to user groups or assignment groups.
 Protection for applications by identifying and restricting access to application files and data does not describe an update set. This behavior aligns with application scoping, which controls access to application resources.
 Field mappings that define relationships between import set fields and fields in a target table do not describe an update set. This behavior aligns with transform maps used during data imports.
questions.topic: Data Migration and Integration - System update sets

questions.question: Where do users switch their instance to display a different colored theme?
options: All > My Company Applications > Create New
questions.explanation:
Navigating to the Theme Module from the User Menu allows users to update their personal display settings, including choosing a different colored theme. The Theme preference lives inside user level UI settings.
 Navigating to the Profile module from the User Menu does not allow users to change their theme. The Profile area is focused on user information and related settings.
 Navigating to Workflow Studio does not allow users to change their theme. Workflow Studio is used to design and manage flows, playbooks, and related automation assets.
 Navigating to My Company Applications > Create New does not allow users to change their theme. The My Company Applications area is used for managing and configuring company applications.
questions.topic: Instance Configuration - Personalizing/customizing the instance

questions.question: Which feature enforces field rules regardless of whether data is entered through a form?
questions.explanation:
Data policies enforce field rules at the server level, so they apply to data entered into a form for data consistency.
 UI policies do not enforce rules during imports. UI policies only control field behavior in the user interface when a form is being used.
 Client scripts do not enforce rules during imports. Client scripts run in the browser and only execute when the user is interacting with a form.
 Dictionary attributes do not enforce conditional field rules. Dictionary Attributes define field characteristics such as default values or behaviors at the dictionary level.
questions.topic: Configuring Applications for Collaboration - Advanced Form Configuration

questions.question: Which information does the Security Configuration page in Security Center display?
options: Audit history of all administrative changes
questions.explanation:
Guidance for addressing configuration risks includes the remediation recommendations that Security Center provides when it detects configuration issues. These recommendations outline the steps an administrator can take to resolve identified risks, including configuration adjustments, activation or deactivation of features, or changes to system settings. This guidance helps ensure that customers can take informed action to improve their security posture without relying solely on automated corrections or external documentation.
 The instance's configuration compliance score represents the calculated percentage of configuration settings that adhere to recommended Security Center hardening guidelines. This score summarizes the instance's alignment with best-practice configurations, reflects improvements or degradations in configuration health over time, and provides administrators with a measurable indicator of compliance. By highlighting the degree of adherence to recommended settings, the score helps guide prioritization of remediation activities.
 Real-time authentication and login activity refers to monitoring user sign-ins, failed login attempts, and authentication-related behaviors. These events are not displayed on the Security Configuration page; instead, they are tracked through identity and authentication-focused modules, such as Identity Center or login history records. Authentication data is operational rather than configuration-based, and therefore falls outside the scope of the configuration risk analysis performed in Security Center.
 Audit history of administrative changes captures system modifications such as updates to configurations, script changes, table alterations, or other administrative actions. These changes are recorded in platform update logs, including the Customer Updates table, and can be reviewed through update set history, audit logs, or change tracking tools. Because audit activity documents administrative modification history rather than configuration compliance, it is not included on the Security Configuration page.
 Incoming email filtering details include information related to email processing, spam detection, and filtering rules applied to inbound messages. These capabilities are provided through the platform's email and notification subsystems, which manage address filtering, spam scoring, and email rule evaluation. Because email filtering pertains to message processing rather than configuration compliance or instance hardening, this information is not presented on the Security Configuration page.
questions.topic: Database Management and Platform Security - Security Center

questions.question: How is a set of predefined options for a field configured on a form?
options: By right-clicking on the form header and selecting Configure Related Lists
By navigating to the Dictionary Entry and modifying the Choice List Specification
By right-clicking on the field and selecting Configure Choices
By navigating to the variable and modifying the question choices
questions.explanation:
Enabling a set of predefined options in a form is done by navigating to the Dictionary Entry and modifying the Choice List Specification. navigating to the Dictionary Entry by opening the System Definition application and selecting the Dictionary module.
 Enabling a set of predefined options in a form is also done by right-clicking on the field and selecting Configure Choices. Once there, the Administrator needs to select Dictionary.
 Right Clicking directly on the field and selecting Configure Choices opens the sys_choice record, which allows you to modify the choices. Configuring Related Lists from the form header modifies which related lists appear on the form, but this approach does not modify the choice list for a field.
 Modifying question choices for a variable applies only to Service Catalog variables and does not configure the choice list for a field on a standard form.
questions.topic: Configuring Applications for Collaboration - Advanced Form Configuration

questions.question: Which role is required to add a related list to a form?
questions.explanation:
The Personalize Form [personalize_form] role is required to configure a form layout, including adding, removing, or rearranging related lists on a form.
 The Form Admin [form_admin] is not the role that grants permission to add related lists. The form_admin roles allows users to create a form section.
 The ITIL User [itil] role does not grant permissions to modify form configuration. The itil role is used for users who work on task-based records such as incidents and changes.
 TheTemplate Editor [template_editor] role does not control form configuration. The template_editor role is used to create and manage templates that populate form fields with predefined values.
questions.topic: Configuring Applications for Collaboration - Form Configuration

questions.question: What does an Administrator use to view, install and manage applications in the instance?
questions.explanation:
The Application Manager module allows administrators to view, install, and manage applications in the instance. It provides tools for managing app versions, dependencies, and installation status.
 The System Logs module does not allow administrators to view, install, or manage applications. The system logs module provides access to log records such as system events, warnings, and errors.
 Scheduled jobs do not allow administrators to manage applications. Scheduled jobs are used to view and run automated background jobs on a scheduled basis.
 Data policies do not allow administrators to view, install, or manage applications. Data policies enforce field requirements when data is entered into the platform.
questions.topic: Instance Configuration - Installing applications and plugins

questions.question: Which feature organizes fields on a form into collapsible groups?
questions.explanation:
The Sections feature organize fields on a form into collapsible groups. Sections help structure the form so users can view related fields together.
 A related list does not organize fields on a form into collapsible groups. Related Lists display records from other tables that are associated with the current record.
 The activity stream does not organize fields on a form into collapsible groups. The activity stream displays comments, work notes, and system updates related to the record.
 List Layout does not organize fields on a form into collapsible groups. List Layout configures which fields appear as columns in a list view.
questions.topic: Configuring Applications for Collaboration - List and Form anatomy

questions.question: What does the REQ number represent in the Service Catalog Fulfillment Process?
options: The tasks assigned to fulfillment teams
The entire request submitted by the user
The set of questions the requester answers to provide item details
The individual items that were ordered
questions.explanation:
The REQ number identifies the overall Service Catalog request. It serves as the parent record that tracks the entire order the user submitted. The REQ number does not represent the individual items that were ordered. This is actually describing a Requested Item (RITM) record. An RITM reflects each specific catalog item included within a request.
 The REQ number does not represent the tasks assigned to fulfillment teams. This is actually describing Service Catalog Task (SCTASK) records. SCTASKS are the tasks created from an RITM and assigned to groups or individuals.
 The REQ number does not represent the set of questions the requester answers to provide item details. This is actually describing variables. Variables capture user input on the catalog item form, not the REQ itself.
questions.topic: Self Service & Automation - Service Catalog

questions.question: What does Virtual Agent use to define conversations that users can interact with?
questions.explanation:
Topics define the conversational flows that users interact with in Virtual Agent. They structure the steps, questions, and logic used during a chat session.
 Knowledge Articles do not define Virtual Agent conversations. Knowledge Articles provide informational content that users can read to troubleshoot or learn information.
 Catalog items do not define Virtual Agent conversations. Catalog items allow users to request goods or services through the Service Catalog. Actions do not define Virtual Agent conversations. Actions are reusable automation steps that can be used within flows.
questions.topic: Self Service & Automation - Virtual Agent

questions.question: What does the maturity level represent for a Security Best Practice?
options: The access control requirements needed to complete the best practice
The level of encryption required for data protected by the best practice
The number of security tasks associated with the best practice
The order of impact and effort required to implement the best practice
questions.explanation:
Maturity level represents the staged progression used to categorize best practices by their relative impact and implementation effort. Security Center organizes best practices into maturity phases-Build a foundation, Enhance the experience, Optimize the functionality, and Add advanced features-to help organizations prioritize improvements. Lower-level maturity stages include foundational changes, while higher levels introduce more advanced or specialized enhancements. This structure guides administrators in planning security posture improvements in logical, progressive steps.
 Encryption requirements are not used to determine maturity level. Though some best practices relate to encryption or data protection, maturity levels categorize best practices by impact and complexity rather than technical attributes such as encryption strength or method. Encryption needs vary widely across individual best practices and do not indicate maturity progression.
 Access control requirements are not part of the maturity level classification. While administrators may need certain roles or permissions to carry out changes recommended by a best practice, maturity levels are not based on ACLS or role assignments. Instead, maturity levels describe the progressive security improvement approach used by the organization.
 The number of security tasks attached to a best practice does not determine maturity level. Security tasks are user-created records used to delegate or track implementation work, whereas maturity level is a predefined classification based on the best practice's impact and complexity. A best practice may have many or few tasks regardless of its maturity tier.
questions.topic: Database Management and Platform Security - Security Center

questions.question: Which interfaces does an Administrator use to configure a form?
questions.explanation:
Form design can be used to configure a form by organizing fields and sections on a form using a drag-and-drop interface.
 Form builder can be used to configure a form by managing layout, components, and form behavior in a guided configuration interface. Form template cannot be used to configure a form. Form templates are used to pre-populate field values when creating a new record.
 Form formatter cannot be used to configure a form. Form formatters add specialized UI components to a form.
questions.topic: Configuring Applications for Collaboration - Form Configuration

questions.question: An Administrator wants to verify records as part of the save operation, prior to the database commit. Which 'When to run' option does the Administrator use for the business rule?
questions.explanation:
The Administrator uses the before option. This option determines when a business rule runs after the user submits the form but before any action is taken on the record in the database. This timing allows the rule to verify or modify data prior to the database commit.
 The Administrator does not use the after option. The after option does not determine when records are verified prior to the database commit. After business rules run after the user submits the form and after actions are taken on the record in the database.
 The Administrator does not use the async option. The async option does not determine when records are verified prior to the database commit. Async business Rules run after the user submits the form or after a scheduled job created from the rule runs.
 The Administrator does not use the display option. The display option does not determine when records are verified during the save operation. Display business rules run before the form is presented to the user, just after data is read from the database.
questions.topic: Data Migration and Integration - Business Rules

questions.question: Which scripting type is used to control how a form behaves when a user interacts with it?
questions.explanation:
A client-side script is used to control how a form behaves when a user interacts with it. Client-side scripts run in the user's browser and control form behavior such as visibility, mandatory status, and validation.
 A scheduled job is not used to control form behavior. Scheduled jobs run scripts at defined intervals without user interaction.
 A Server-side script is not used to control how a form behaves during user interaction. Server-side scripts run on the server or database to perform record and table operations.
 A Transform Map is not used to control form behavior. Transform maps are used to map and transform imported data into target tables.
questions.topic: Data Migration and Integration - Scripting in ServiceNow

questions.question: Which interface displays visualizations to allow users to make data-driven decisions?
questions.explanation:
A dashboard displays visualizations to help users make data-driven decisions. It shows reports, charts, and widgets in a consolidated view.
 The activity stream does not display visualizations for data-driven decisions. The activity stream shows real-time updates, comments, and field changes on a record.
 The Service Catalog does not display visualizations for data-driven decisions. The service catalog enables users to request items and services through structured catalog items.
 A Knowledge Article does not display visualizations to support data-driven decisions. Knowledge articles provide informational content that users read to learn about the company's procedures, troubleshooting steps, or reference material.
questions.topic: Instance Configuration - Common user interfaces in the Platform

questions.question: What does the Virtual Agent messaging interface provide?
options: A place for users to update ACL roles
questions.explanation:
The Virtual Agent messaging interface provides a conversational self-service experience. It gives users an automated chat that helps them find information and complete simple tasks through guided interactions.
 The Virtual Agent messaging interface does not allow users to update access control list (ACL) roles. ACL management happens in the System Security application, where admins configure role-based access controls.
 The Virtual Agent messaging interface does not provide tools for building integrations. Integrations are created using IntegrationHub.
 The Virtual Agent messaging interface does not serve as a workspace for fulfillment teams. Fulfillment teams typically work in Workspaces like Agent Workspace or Customer Service Management (CSM) Workspace.
questions.topic: Self Service & Automation - Virtual Agent

questions.question: How does a user leave feedback on a knowledge article?
questions.explanation:
Flagging the article is a valid method of providing feedback. This alerts the knowledge manager that the article may be incorrect, outdated, or unclear.
 Star ratings provide direct feedback about the quality or usefulness of a knowledge article. This helps knowledge managers evaluate article performance.
 Impersonating a user is not a way to leave feedback on a knowledge article. Impersonation allows administrators to temporarily view the platform from another user's perspective to test permissions and functionality.
 Subscribing to an article is not a method for leaving feedback on a knowledge article. Subscribing notifies a user when the article is updated.
questions.topic: Self Service & Automation - Knowledge Management

questions.question: What tracks and measures a specific metric over time using historical snapshots and trend data?
questions.explanation:
A Performance Analytics Indicator tracks and measures a specific metric over time using historical snapshots and trend data. Indicators allow users to analyze performance trends and monitor progress toward goals.
 Data visualizations do not track and measure a metric over time using historical snapshots. Data visualizations display data graphically, such as charts or graphs, but do not store historical trend data.
 A Dashboard does not track and measure a metric over time using historical snapshots. A Dashboard provides a single page where multiple reports and visualizations are displayed together.
 A table does not track and measure a metric over time using historical snapshots. A table stores and organizes records and fields that hold the underlying data used in reports and analytics.
questions.topic: Configuring Applications for Collaboration - Visualizations, Dashboards, and Platform Analytics

questions.question: Which features can be used to activate or implement applications or application features in the ServiceNow Platform?
questions.explanation:
Plugins allow users to access applications and application functionality on the ServiceNow platform.
 The ServiceNow store has a catalog of applications that can be downloaded and used on the ServiceNow platform.
 UI Policies cannot be used to activate or implement applications or application features. UI Policies are used to conditionally make fields displayed, hidden, or mandatory.
 Access Controls cannot be used to activate or implement applications or application features. Access Controls are used for application security.
 Business Rules cannot be used to activate or implement applications or application features. Business Rules execute server-side logic when records are inserted, updated, or deleted.
questions.topic: Instance Configuration - Installing applications and plugins

questions.question: What allows an inherited field to behave differently on a child table?
questions.explanation:
A dictionary override allows an inherited field from a parent table to behave differently on a child table. A dictionary override record on the child table overrides specific inherited dictionary attributes without modifying the parent field.
 A UI policy does not allow an inherited field to behave differently across tables. UI Policies only change field behavior on a specific form based on conditions.
 A client script does not allow an inherited field to behave differently across tables. Client scripts execute logic in the browser to perform client- side actions on a form.
 A form layout does not allow an inherited field to behave differently across tables. Form layout controls the placement and arrangement of fields on a form.
questions.topic: Configuring Applications for Collaboration - Advanced Form Configuration

questions.question: Which table relationships are represented as many-to-many relationships in the ServiceNow data schema?
questions.explanation:
User and Group represent a many-to-many relationship because users can belong to multiple groups, and each group can contain multiple users. Records from both tables are visible to one another through a related list, which reflects this bidirectional relationship.
 User and Role represent a many-to-many relationship because a user can be assigned multiple roles, and a single role can be assigned to multiple users. The related lists on both tables make the associated records visible, confirming the many-to-many relationship.
 Incident and Task do not represent a many-to-many relationship because Incident extends the Task table through table inheritance. This is a parent-child relationship rather than a relationship managed through a many-to-many table.
 Location and Asset do not form a many-to-many relationship because assets typically reference a single location. This creates a one-to-many relationship, where one location can be associated with many assets.
 Catalog Task and Requested Item do not represent a many-to-many relationship because each catalog task is associated with one requested item. This results in a one-to-many relationship.
questions.topic: Database Management and Platform Security - Data Schema

questions.question: Which table stores connection data for CI?
questions.explanation:
The cmdb_rel_ci table stores Configuration Item (CI) relationship data. It contains all the records that describe how configuration items relate to one another, including dependency chains, containment relationships, and hierarchical parent-child structures. Administrators rely on this table to maintain accurate and traceable Cl interactions across the Configuration Management Database (CMDB).
 The cmdb table stores metadata that defines the core structure and operational framework of the CMDB. Instead of holding relationship instances, it contains system-level information used to support CMDB functionality. Since it does not store dependency, containment, or parent-child relationship records, administrators cannot use this table to manage Cl relationships.
 The cmdb_ci table serves as the base class for all configuration items and stores Cl attributes such as identifiers, classification, and operational metadata. Its purpose is to represent individual Cls, not the relationships between them. Since it contains Cl-level information rather than relational mappings, it is not used by administrators to record Cl relationship data.
 The cmdb_class_info table contains descriptive and structural metadata about CMDB classes, including class hierarchy, inheritance patterns, and class definitions. It is designed to support the understanding and management of CMDB class architecture, not to store Cl relationship instances.
questions.topic: Database Management and Platform Security - CMDB and CSDM

questions.question: Which feature provides server-side and client-side JavaScript classes and methods for building custom functionality?
questions.explanation:
Application Programming Interfaces (APIs) provide JavaScript classes and methods that can be used within scripts to define functionality and interact with the ServiceNow platform. APIs such as GlideRecord and GlideSystem allow developers to query tables, manipulate records, and access system information programmatically.
 UI Policies do not provide scripting classes or methods. UI Policies conditionally control form field behavior such as visibility, mandatory status, and read-only state.
 Business rules do not provide reusable scripting methods. Business Rules define when server-side scripts execute during database operations such as insert, update, or delete, but they rely on existing APIs rather than creating them.
 Client Scripts do not provide JavaScript classes or methods. Client Scripts execute JavaScript in response to form events such as onLoad, onChange, or onSubmit, and they use available client-side APIs like g_form.
questions.topic: Data Migration and Integration - Scripting in ServiceNow

questions.question: What are record triggers in Flow Designer?
questions.explanation:
The Created record trigger is available in Flow Designer. The Created trigger fires a flow when a new record is added to a table. This behavior is specific to Flow Designer triggers and initiates automation when records are first generated.
 The Updated record trigger is available in Flow Designer. It fires a flow when an existing record is modified. This ensures actions run in response to changes made to a record.
 The Retired state is not a record trigger available in Flow Designer. This term applies to the lifecycle of knowledge articles, indicating an article is no longer available to end users.
 The Before condition is not a record trigger available in Flow Designer. This condition is a Business Rule timing option that determines when a business rule runs relative to the database action.
 onChange is not a record trigger available in Flow Designer. onChange belongs to Client Scripts and controls actions that occur when a field value changes on the client-side form.
questions.topic: Self Service & Automation - Workflow Studio

questions.question: Which type of Business Rule runs after data is read from the database, but before the form is shown?
questions.explanation:
The display option determines when a business rule runs after data is read from the database but before the form is presented to the user. A display business rule is used to prepare data for form display.
 The onChange option does not determine when a business rule runs. The onChange option is a client script type that runs when a field value changes on a form.
 The onLoad option does not determine when a Business Rule runs. The onLoad option is a client script type that runs when a form loads in the browser.
 The after option does not determine when a business rule runs before the form is shown. An after business rule runs after actions are taken on the record in the database.
questions.topic: Data Migration and Integration - Business Rules

questions.question: In an instance configured with Default Deny (glide.sm.default_mode = Deny), what happens when no explicit table or field ACL matches a requested record operation?
options: The platform grants the operation because no specific ACL exists to restrict the action.
The system blocks the request until the user elevates to the security_admin role.
The wildcard table ACLs deny the operation unless admin access or another ACL explicitly grants it.
The platform prompts an administrator to create a new ACL before processing the request.
questions.explanation:
With Default Deny enabled, when no explicit table or field ACL matches a requested operation, the platform falls back to the out-of-box wildcard table ACLs for that operation. In this mode, those wildcard ACLs restrict CRUD on all tables and the operation is denied unless the user is admin or another specific ACL grants access to the target object. The admin role can override access controls in the base system, which is why admins typically pass this check while non-admin users do not.
 By default, the wildcard ACLS are the only rules that read the glide.sm.default_mode setting; administrators may extend similar behavior to other operations only by creating additional ACLs that explicitly check the property. Note that in modern instances this property is set to Deny by default, and once set to Deny you cannot revert it to Allow.
 The platform does not prompt administrators to auto-create ACLs. Instead, administrators manually configure ACLS and related high-security settings, and must elevate to the security_admin role to make those changes.
 The security_admin role is an elevated configuration role used to modify ACLs; it is not a runtime requirement evaluated by the ACL engine when deciding access to a record or field.
questions.topic: Database Management and Platform Security - Application/Access Control

questions.question: When is the hardening compliance score calculated in Security Center?
options: After the clone of the instance
After the installation of the instance
On the first day of each month
After the application of a hotfix patch
After every upgrade of the platform
questions.explanation:
The hardening compliance score is calculated in Security Center when the application is installed or reinstalled, ensuring the system immediately evaluates how closely the instance aligns with recommended security hardening settings. This initial calculation provides a baseline compliance score and confirms whether critical hardening controls are enabled or require adjustments.
 The hardening compliance score is calculated in Security Center when the monthly cycle runs on the first day of each month. This scheduled recalculation ensures continuous monitoring of compliance by reassessing all hardening rules and identifying new deviations that may have appeared since the previous month.
 The hardening compliance score is calculated in Security Center when users manually trigger the Update score button. This option allows administrators to immediately refresh the score after making configuration changes, enabling quick validation of improvements or detection of new compliance gaps without waiting for the monthly run.
 The hardening compliance score is not calculated in Security Center when an instance clone occurs. Cloning does not automatically initiate a recalculation, which means that the compliance score may not reflect the current state unless the system reaches the monthly recalculation point or the administrator initiates a manual update.
 The hardening compliance score is not calculated in Security Center when a hotfix patch is applied. Hotfixes do not trigger the compliance scoring process, so recalculation still depends on the scheduled monthly run or a manual refresh initiated by the administrator.
 The hardening compliance score is not calculated in Security Center when a platform upgrade completes. Upgrades alone do not trigger recalculation, and administrators must rely on the standard monthly recalculation or manually update the score if an immediate assessment is required.

questions.question: Which options determine when a Business Rule runs?
questions.explanation:
The display option determines when a Business Rule runs before the form is presented to the user, just after the data is read from the database. Display business rules control behavior before the form is shown.
 The async option determines when a Business Rule runs asynchronously after the database operation completes. Async business rules run in the background without delaying the user action.
 The OnSubmit option does not determine when a Business Rule runs. OnSubmit is a Client Script type that runs when a form is submitted.
 The Table option does not determine when a Business Rule runs. The Table option specifies which table the Business Rule applies to.

questions.question: Which type of Visual Task Board is used to manage a filtered set of task records?

 A Freeform Board is not used to manage a filtered set of task records. Freeform Boards are manually created and are not tied to a list or filter of records.
 A Guided Board is not used to manage a filtered set of task records. Guided Boards are designed to support a structured workflow process with predefined lanes.
 Line is not a type of Visual Task Board. Line is a data visualization type used in reports and dashboards to display trends over time.

questions.question: Which feature does a System Administrator use to test functionality as another user?

 The System Administrator does not use the Global Search feature to impersonate another user. Global Search is used to find records and information across the platform.
 The System Administrator does not use The Application Navigator feature to impersonate another user. Application Navigator is used to browse and open applications and modules in the platform.
 The System Administrator does not use the History feature to impersonate another user. History provides a list of recently accessed records and modules for quick navigation.

questions.question: Which capability does a Manager use to automate the approval process?
questions.explanation:
Flow Designer can automate approval processes by using flows that route requests to approvers based on defined conditions. It is designed for building automated workflows without writing code, including approvals.
 Catalog Builder does not automate approval processes. It is a guided interface used to create and manage catalog items without scripting.
 UI Builder does not automate approval processes. It is used to build and configure workspace and experience pages for the Now Experience interface.
 Virtual Agent does not automate approval processes. It provides automated conversational experiences that help users answer questions and complete simple tasks.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a Workspace?
options: To create a conversational experience to increase user's ability to troubleshoot problems
To give agents a streamlined interface for managing and completing their work
questions.explanation:
The purpose of a Workspace is to give agents a streamlined interface for managing and completing their work. Workspaces provide agents and fulfillers with a modern, streamlined interface that centralizes tasks, records, lists, and tools to help them complete their work efficiently. Workspaces are designed for productivity, guided experiences, and quick access to the data agents need.
 Ordering items and services does not describe the purpose of a Workspace. This is actually describing the Service Catalog, which allows users to browse available items and submit requests for goods and services.
 Building application files does not describe the purpose of a Workspace. This is actually describing Studio, which developers use to build and configure application files like tables, script includes, and flows.
 Creating a conversational experience to increase user's ability to troubleshoot problems does not describe the purpose of a Workspace. This is actually describing Virtual Agent, which provides automated conversational assistance to help users troubleshoot issues and find answers.

questions.question: What happens if a user fails a table-level Read ACL rule?
options: The system logs a warning but still allows the user to access the record.
The system denies access to the field but still allows access to the rest of the record.
The system denies access to the record and prevents the user from viewing it.
The system displays a warning message asking the user if they want to continue.
questions.explanation:
The system denies access to the record and prevents the user from viewing it. This is because failing a table Access Control rule (ACL) blocks all access to the record itself. Table ACLS control permissions at the record level, and a failed check stops the user from retrieving or viewing the record.
 The system does not deny access to the field but still allows access to the rest of the record. This only happens when a user fails a field-level ACL, not a table ACL. A failed table ACL blocks access to the entire record, not just individual fields.
 The system does not display a warning message asking the user if they want to continue. ACL rule failures do not generate user prompts or warnings. ACLs enforce access automatically and do not allow users to bypass or confirm access.
 The system does not log a warning but still allows the user to access the record. ACL evaluation does not permit access when a table ACL fails. The system stops the access request and does not allow record.

questions.question: What is assigned to a user to grant permission to access features within the platform?
questions.explanation:
Roles are assigned to users to grant permission to access features within the ServiceNow platform. Roles define what a user can see and do across applications and modules.
 Groups do not grant users access to platform features. Groups organize users for task assignments and approvals, and while they can contain roles, the roles themselves provide access.
 Access Control List (ACL) Rules do not grant users access to platform features. ACL Rules enforce record-level security by determining who can create, read, update, or delete data.
 UI Policies do not grant users access to platform features. UI Policies control client-side form behavior by making fields visible, mandatory, or read-only.

questions.question: What is the goal of the Shared Responsibility Model in ServiceNow?
options: To assess configuration risk and recommend remediation
To clarify accountability and uphold security and privacy
To preserve CMDB integrity and sustain effectiveness
To automate tests and validate the instance after changes
questions.explanation:
The goal of the Shared Responsibility Model is define clear accountability across customers and uphold security and privacy. This model clarifies who does what across security and privacy so risk is minimized and all parties meet their obligations: customers act as data controllers (configuring access, classifying data, enforcing policies in-instance), ServiceNow operates and secures the platform as the data processor, and underlying providers (colocation/hyperscalers) have their own clearly delineated duties; this explicit division of accountability is the point of the model in the Zurich release and is framed around helping organizations fulfill security and privacy commitments.
 The goal of the Shared Responsibility Model is not to assess configuration risk or recommend remediation steps. Those capabilities belong to Security Center and Configuration Compliance, which identify configuration weaknesses, calculate compliance and hardening scores, and guide remediation efforts. The Shared Responsibility Model does not perform assessments or generate remediation tasks; instead, it defines who is responsible for using the platform's security capabilities and for remediating risks identified by those tools.
 The goal of the Shared Responsibility Model is not to provide automated testing capabilities. Automated testing is the purpose of the Automated Test Framework (ATF), which enables customers to create and run regression tests, validate platform behavior after changes, and support upgrade readiness. While testing is part of the customer's responsibilities under the Shared Responsibility Model, the model itself does not supply testing functionality; it only defines that customers are accountable for verifying their configurations and customizations through tools like ATF.
 The goal of the Shared Responsibility Model is not to maintain the integrity or effectiveness of the Configuration Management Database (CMDB). CMDB maintenance is supported by capabilities such as CMDB Health, CMDB Workspace, and the reconciliation and governance tools used to manage data quality. The Shared Responsibility Model clarifies that customers are responsible for ensuring CMDB data accuracy and completeness, but it does not provide the mechanisms to maintain or measure data quality. Instead, it establishes who is accountable for applying and governing these CMDB tools and processes.

questions.question: Which tab allows a board owner to edit the settings for a Visual Task Board?

 The Info tab does not allow editing task board settings. The Info tab displays information about the board, such as name, type, owner, and filter details.
 The Labels tab does not allow editing task board settings. The Labels tab is used to apply and manage labels to visually distinguish and filter tasks.
 The Activity tab does not allow editing task board settings. The Activity tab displays all activities related to the cards on the board.

questions.question: Which components are built using Workflow Studio?
questions.explanation:
Flows can be built using Workflow Studio. Flows allow administrators to automate processes through a sequence of actions.
 Playbooks can be built using Workflow Studio. Playbooks guide users through structured activities that support process completion. Workspaces cannot be built using Workflow Studio. Workspaces are created and configured using Workspace Builder or UI Builder.
 UI Policies cannot be built using Workflow Studio. UI Policies are created in the UI Policies module under System UI.
 Dashboards cannot be built using Workflow Studio. Dashboards are created in the Dashboards module and display visualizations such as reports and performance widgets.

questions.question: Which table does the Incident table extend from?
questions.explanation:
The Incident table extends from the Task table. This makes the Incident table a child class of the Task table, meaning it inherits all standard task fields such as assignment, state, priority, workflow properties, and auditing features. By extending Task, Incident gains core task management functionality and adds its own incident-specific fields. This relationship allows Incidents to participate in the common task framework, reporting structures, while having independent fields like, resolution information and categorization.
 The Incident table does not extend from the Problem table. Like the incident table, the Problem table is another child class of the Task table. Because both extend Task independently, neither is a parent or child of the other and do not share a class inheritance relationship.
 The Incident table does not extend from the Change table. Like the Problem table and Incident table, the Change Request table is also a separate child class of the Task table. It provides structure for planned modifications to IT infrastructure and includes lifecycle stages such as planning, approval, testing, and implementation. While Incidents may generate Changes or be associated with them during remediation, they do not inherit fields or behaviors from the Change table.
 The Incident table does not extend from the cmdb_ci table. The cmdb_ci table is its own base table within the Configuration Management Database (CMDB) hierarchy. This table does not participate in the Task hierarchy and is not a parent to any task-related tables. Incidents commonly reference cmdb_ci records through fields like Configuration item, but they do not inherit structure or behavior from the CMDB. The cmdb_citable sits at the root of the configuration item (CI) class hierarchy, separate from all Task-derived tables.

questions.question: Which module in the Service Catalog application is used to create catalog items?
questions.explanation:
The Maintain Items module is used to create, configure, and manage catalog items in the Service Catalog. It provides access to all catalog item records, allowing administrators to build new items and modify existing ones.
 Catalog Client Scripts are not used to create catalog items. This module refers to scripts that run client-side on catalog forms to control field behavior and form interaction.
 User Criteria is not used to create catalog items. This module defines rules that determine which users can view or access specific catalog items or knowledge articles.
 Variable Sets are not used to create catalog items. This module refers to reusable groups of variables that can be attached to catalog items or record producers, but they do not create or maintain the catalog item records.

questions.question: How do Virtual Agent help users?
questions.explanation:
Virtual Agent can help users passwords. It guides users through simple automated steps to complete common support tasks. Virtual Agent can help users submit catalog requests. It guides users through requesting items or services using conversational prompts. Virtual Agent cannot help users in building dashboards. Dashboards are created and configured using the Dashboards module. Virtual Agent cannot help users in configuring access control list (ACL) rules. ACL rules are managed by administrators in the Access Control module.
 Virtual Agent cannot help users write knowledge articles. Knowledge articles are created and edited in the Knowledge Management application by contributors or knowledge managers.

questions.question: What allows an administrator to view the list of plugins that are currently installed on the instance?

 System Diagnostics does not allow administrators to view installed plugins. System Diagnostics is used to review system logs, health checks, and performance information.
 Script includes do not allow administrators to view installed plugins. Script includes store reusable server-side JavaScript functions.
 Data sources do not allow administrators to view installed plugins. Data sources are used to define where imported data comes from when creating an import set.

questions.question: Which configuration checkbox enables scripting within a Business Rule?
questions.explanation:
The advanced field determines whether a Business Rule can be configured to run for specific database operations such as insert, update, or delete. Marking the advanced field as true allows more granular control over when the rule executes.
 The accessible from field does not determine when a Business Rule runs. Accessible from controls where a record can be accessed, such as from all application scopes or only specific ones.
 The filter conditions field does not determine which database operations trigger a business rule. Filter conditions define the criteria that the fields on the selected table must meet for the rule to execute.
 The order field does not determine which database operations trigger a Business Rule. Order controls the sequence in which business rules are evaluated.
